glosses: To end; to come to an end.

examples.text: The story concluded with a moral.

He inveighed against the folly of making oneself liable for the debts of others; vented many bitter execrations against the brother; and concluded with wishing something could be done for the unfortunate family.

glosses: To bring to an end; to close; to finish.

glosses: To come to a conclusion, to a final decision.

examples.text: From the evidence, I conclude that this man was murdered.
No man can certainly conclude God's love or hatred to any person by anything that befalls him.

glosses: To make a final determination or judgment concerning; to judge; to decide.

examples.text: But no frail man, however great or high, / Can be concluded blest before he die.

glosses: To shut off; to restrain; to limit; to estop; to bar.

examples.text: The defendant is concluded by his own plea.

glosses: To shut up; to enclose.

examples.text: The very person of Christ [was] concluded within the grave.

glosses: To include; to comprehend; to shut up together; to embrace; to confine.

examples.text:
Banisht the Court? Let me be banisht Life;
 Since the chief end of Life is there concluded:

glosses: A cause:
That which causes something: an efficient cause, a proximate cause.

examples.text: The reason this tree fell is that it had rotted.
There is a reason why so many should be symmetrical: The selective advantage in a symmetrical complex is enjoyed by all the subunits[…]

glosses: A cause:
A motive for an action or a determination.

examples.text: The reason I robbed the bank was that I needed the money.
If you don't give me a reason to go with you, I won't.
This is the reason why he proposes to offer a libation, to atone for the abuse of the day by their diversions.
Ralph Touchett, for reasons best known to himself, had seen fit to say that Gilbert Osmond was not a good fellow[…]

glosses: A cause:

examples.text: I have forgotten the reason he gave for not travelling by air. I felt sure that it was not the correct reason, and that he suffered from a heart trouble which he kept to himself.

examples.text: Still my spirit was not broken. I indulged the anticipation of escape, and that speedily. It was impossible, I reasoned, that men could be so unjust as to detain me as a slave, when the truth of my case was known.
